skill.name: skill-installer
skill.description: Install Codex skills from curated OpenAI lists or GitHub repository paths, including private repositories with existing credentials.
skill.summary: Install Codex skills from curated lists or GitHub paths into the local skills directory.
skill.author: openai

security_audit.summary: The network, environment, filesystem, and git subprocess findings are mostly confirmed and match the installer purpose. Several Markdown backtick and GitHub path findings are false positives, and zip extraction includes a path traversal guard. The main residual risk is installing unreviewed remote skill content into the active Codex skills directory.

remediation.suggestion: Add a confirmation step that names the repository, ref, paths, and destination before installing non-curated skills.

remediation.issue: Installed skills are only checked for SKILL.md
remediation.suggestion: Add optional safety checks that list scripts, network use, and prompt-injection indicators before copying files.
Document that tokens should be read-only or fine-grained and should only be used for trusted repositories.
Keep subprocess calls shell-free and display the exact repository and ref before git fallback runs.

semantic_findings.description: The installer copies user-selected GitHub content into the Codex skills directory after only checking that SKILL.md exists. A malicious repository can persist new instructions or scripts that load after Codex restarts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented behavior and copy operation show remote skill content is installed without safety review.

content.value_statement: Developers need a repeatable way to discover and add Codex skills. This skill lists curated options and installs selected skills from GitHub into the local skills folder.
actual_capabilities: Lists curated skills from the OpenAI skills repository.
Installs skills from GitHub repository paths or GitHub tree URLs.
Supports private repositories through existing git credentials or GitHub tokens.
Installs multiple skill paths in one command when requested.
Supports branch, destination, install method, and destination name options.
Checks that a selected directory contains SKILL.md before copying it.
limitations: It only supports GitHub sources for remote installation.
Network access and git credentials may be required.
It does not review the safety of installed skill content.
Codex must be restarted before new skills are available.

use_cases.title: Add a curated productivity skill
use_cases.description: Find available curated skills and install one into the default Codex skills directory.

use_cases.title: Roll out an internal skill
use_cases.description: Install a team-owned skill from a private GitHub repository using existing credentials.

use_cases.title: Prepare a managed workstation
use_cases.description: Install several approved skills into a chosen skills directory during setup.

prompt_templates.prompt: List the curated Codex skills that are available and show which ones are already installed.

prompt_templates.prompt: Install the curated skill named documentation-helper into my default Codex skills folder.

prompt_templates.title: Install from a Private Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Install the skill at skills/release-notes from my private GitHub repository acme/internal-skills.

prompt_templates.title: Install Multiple Paths from a Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Install skills/linting and skills/code-review from acme/dev-skills using the release branch and git method.

output_examples.output: The assistant shows a numbered list of curated skills and marks entries that are already installed.

output_examples.input: Install a skill from a GitHub tree URL.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs the installer, reports the installed skill path, and tells the user to restart Codex.
The assistant uses available credentials, falls back to git when needed, and reports any permission error clearly.

best_practices: Install skills only from repositories you trust and can review.
Use read-only or fine-grained GitHub credentials when private access is needed.
Restart Codex after installation so the new skill is loaded cleanly.
anti_patterns: Do not install skills from unknown repositories without reviewing their files.
Do not use broad GitHub tokens when read-only access is enough.
Do not overwrite existing skill directories unless you intentionally replace them.

faq.question: What does this skill install?
faq.answer: It installs Codex skill directories that contain a SKILL.md file.

faq.question: Can it install from private GitHub repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use existing git credentials or GitHub tokens from the environment.

faq.question: Where are skills installed by default?
faq.answer: They are installed under CODEX_HOME skills, or the default Codex home directory when CODEX_HOME is unset.

faq.question: Does it execute installed skills immediately?
faq.answer: No. The user must restart Codex before installed skills are loaded.

faq.question: Can it install more than one skill at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Multiple repository paths can be provided in one install request.

faq.question: Does it validate skill safety?
faq.answer: No. It checks for SKILL.md, but users should review skill instructions and scripts before installation.
